data.narrative:
Walden Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company currently valued at $1.1B post-money, having raised $300M to date. The company is led by Russ Tedrake, MIT professor and former SVP of Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute. The peer universe comprises 9 comparable private robotics firms (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity among them) valued between $1.0B and $2.3B across Series B through Series F stages, plus one public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $1.1B last post-money valuation, yielding $2.8B. Peer-median benchmarking across seven same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables produces a median of $1.8B with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods triangulate to a low of $1.5B, median of $2.2B, and high of $3.2B.

The $2.2B median implies upside from the current $1.1B valuation but is constrained by the peer universe median sitting below the stage-progression case. Key uncertainties include the extent to which founder pedigree and prior Toyota AI/robotics work command premium positioning within the peer set, and whether capital deployed to date translates to revenue or traction that would justify stage progression acceleration.
